## Purpose

This SOP describes the complete workflow for analyzing soil and
sediment samples for $\delta^{15}$N, $\delta^{13}$C, and elemental C
and N content using the Thermo Scientific Flash IRMS Elemental
Analyzer (EA) coupled to the Delta V Isotope Ratio Mass Spectrometer
(IRMS) through the ConFlo IV continuous-flow interface [@thermo_flashea;
@thermo_deltav]. It covers sample preparation, instrument warm-up,
sequence creation, running the analysis, shutdown, and data reduction.

For general instrument operation, gas checks, and pre-analysis tests,
see [SOP-L208](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd). For the full
data correction workflow (blank, linearity, scale normalization, and
drift correction), see [SOP-L414](SOP-L414-soil-ea-irms.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Soil, sediment, and plant tissue samples analyzed
  for $\delta^{13}$C, $\delta^{15}$N, and elemental concentrations
  (%C, %N) by combustion EA-IRMS in NC (dual reactor) mode
- **Does not apply to:** Sulfur isotope analysis (NCS mode), GasBench
  carbonate analysis (see [SOP-L415](SOP-L415-carbonate-gasbench-irms.qmd)),
  TC/EA hydrogen and oxygen isotope analysis, or liquid samples
- **Location:** Sample preparation in SGM Rm 133; analysis in the
  Oxtoby Environmental Isotope Lab, SGM Rm 135


## Responsibilities

| Role               | Responsibility                                           |
|:-------------------|:---------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI             | Approve methods, ensure training compliance              |
| Lab Manager        | Prepare and verify instrument methods; maintain reactors |
| Super-User         | Supervise trainees; perform minor maintenance            |
| Certified User     | Prepare samples, build sequences, run analyses           |
| Student Researcher | Sample weighing and data reduction (no unsupervised runs)|


## Definitions

- **Blank correction:** Subtraction of the isotopic and elemental
  contribution of an empty tin capsule from each sample signal;
  necessary because capsule tin contributes a small amount of C and N
  [@paul2007; @thermo_flashea].
- **Certified user:** A student, staff, or faculty member qualified to
  prepare samples and run the IRMS without supervision, as designated
  by the lab PI.
- **ConFlo IV:** Interface hub connecting the Flash EA and other
  peripherals to the Delta V IRMS; handles reference-gas delivery and
  peak switching [@thermo_conflo].
- **$\delta^{13}$C:** Stable carbon isotope ratio expressed in per
  mil (‰) relative to Vienna Pee Dee Belemnite (VPDB):
  $\delta^{13}C = (R_\text{sample}/R_\text{standard} - 1) \times 1000$
  where $R = {}^{13}C/{}^{12}C$ [@coplen2011].
- **$\delta^{15}$N:** Stable nitrogen isotope ratio expressed in per
  mil (‰) relative to atmospheric N~2~ (AIR):
  $\delta^{15}N = (R_\text{sample}/R_\text{standard} - 1) \times 1000$
  where $R = {}^{15}N/{}^{14}N$ [@coplen2011].
- **Drift correction:** Adjustment for systematic temporal change in
  measured $\delta$ values during a sequence, estimated from bracketing
  reference materials [@paul2007].
- **Flash EA:** The Thermo Scientific Flash IRMS Elemental Analyzer
  peripheral; combusts samples at 1020 °C in an O~2~ pulse and
  separates N~2~ and CO~2~ chromatographically before delivery to the
  IRMS via the ConFlo IV [@thermo_flashea].
- **Isodat:** Thermo Fisher software for analytical sequence design,
  instrument control, and raw isotope data export [@thermo_isodat].
- **Linearity correction:** Adjustment applied to account for the
  dependence of measured $\delta$ values on peak amplitude at the
  detector [@paul2007].
- **Reference material (RM):** A substance with certified or consensus
  $\delta$ values used to anchor measured values to the VPDB or AIR
  scale; at least two RMs spanning the expected sample range are
  required for two-point scale normalization [@werner2001; @coplen2011].
- **Scale normalization:** Two-point (or multi-point) correction that
  maps measured $\delta$ values to the international isotope-ratio
  scale using certified reference materials [@paul2007; @coplen2011].
- **Super-user:** A staff or faculty member qualified to run the IRMS
  and perform minor maintenance (gas replacement, reactor exchange, etc.).
- **Tin capsule:** 5 × 9 mm pressed-tin container used to encapsulate
  solid samples; tin ignites in the O~2~ pulse, raising combustion
  temperature briefly to ensure complete combustion.
- **Zero-enrichment test:** Reference gas on/off pulses used to verify
  that the IRMS measures consistent $\delta$ values before analysis;
  performed during instrument warm-up.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Pressurized gases:** He, O~2~, N~2~, CO~2~. Verify cylinder
  pressures before each session. He tank pressure must be above
  500 psi, regulated to 50 psi.
- **Hot surfaces:** The Flash EA combustion reactor operates above
  1000 °C. Use caution when handling ash fingers or reactor tubes.
- **Sharps:** Syringes, tweezers, and capsule-crimping tools can cause
  puncture or cut injuries.
- **Chemical:** Chromium oxide, silvered cobaltous/cobaltic oxide, and
  reduced copper used in the reactor packing are irritants; follow
  standard laboratory handling precautions.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### User Responsibilities
The lab manager verifies that methods are working properly, but
**Certified Users** are responsible for preparing their own samples,
creating run sequences, overseeing runs, and conducting data reduction.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Laboratory coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (especially when handling reactor packing
      materials)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-L208](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd) for
instrument-specific emergency procedures and
[SOP-L002](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) for general lab safety.

| Quartz wool                       | 338 22200        | ---                |
| Magnesium perchlorate (Anhydrone) | 281 13102        | ---                |

### Capsules and Weighing Supplies

- Tin capsules (appropriate size for your sample mass)
- Tungsten oxide (WO~3~) -- approximately 2 parts per sample for
  combustion aid (if required by method)
- Aluminum crucibles (for oven-drying soils)
- Weighing paper, cell wells, tweezers, spatulas
- Kimwipes, gloves

### Standard Reference Materials {#sec-standards}

Prepare calibrated internal standards for every batch. Confirm which
standards you need **before** approaching the lab. Standards on hand
(certified values):

| Reference Standard | $\delta^{13}$C (VPDB) | $\delta^{15}$N (AIR) |
|:-------------------|:--------------------:|:-------------------:|
| LOCSS              | --26.66              | 7.30                |
| HOCSS              | --26.27              | 4.42                |
| Urea               | --43.26              | --0.56              |
| USGS24             | --16.05              | ---                 |
| USGS40             | --26.39              | --4.52              |
| USGS41a            | 36.55                | 47.6                |

[@werner2001; @coplen2011]

::: {.callout-important}
Lab standards are shared resources. Do not use them without approval
from a super-user, the lab technician, or the PI. You are expected to
replace what you use.
:::


## Sample Preparation

### Drying and Grinding

1. Weigh soil or sediment samples into aluminum crucibles.
2. Oven-dry at 105 °C until constant mass.
3. Grind dried samples to a fine, homogeneous powder.

### Elemental Pre-screening

Submit a subset of samples to elemental analysis (EA) to determine %C
and %N before committing the full batch. This determines the correct
sample mass to target the optimal signal range.

### Sample Weighing

The target sample mass depends on %C and %N concentrations
[@thermo_flashea]:

| Typical %C    | Target Sample Mass | Notes                           |
|:--------------|:------------------|:--------------------------------|
| > 5% C        | 3--5 mg           | Dilute if signal is too high    |
| 1--5% C       | 7--15 mg          | Standard range                  |
| < 1% C        | 15--25 mg         | May require longer run times    |

1. Fold a tin capsule using tweezers (clean hands; no skin oils).
2. Weigh the target sample mass into the capsule.
3. Add WO~3~ if required for combustion aids.
4. Crimp the capsule tightly so no sample can escape during handling.
5. Place crimped capsules in sequence order in a cell-well plate.
6. Record the exact mass of each sample in the data reduction
   spreadsheet.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip: Clean Tweezers and Capsules
Oils and residue from fingers contaminate tin capsules, introducing
C and N blanks. Handle capsules only with clean, dry tweezers
[@thermo_flashea].
:::


## Instrument Warm-Up and Pre-Analysis Checks

See [SOP-L208](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd) for the complete
warm-up procedure, gas pressure verification, zero-enrichment test,
and linearity check. The Flash EA should be at operating temperature
and passing all pre-analysis tests before loading samples.


## Sequence Design

1. Open Isodat on the acquisition computer [@thermo_isodat].
2. Create a new sequence with the following elements in order:
   - **Empty capsule blanks** (4--6): establish blank baseline
   - **Reference materials** (2--3 each of two or more certified RMs):
     for scale normalization [@coplen2011]
   - **Conditioning samples** (2--3): first samples in the run;
     typically sacrificial or low-priority
   - **Unknown samples** (bracketed by RMs every 10--12 unknowns)
   - **Closing reference materials** (2--3 of each RM): for drift
     correction [@paul2007]
3. Enter sample names, masses, and expected %C/%N for each row.
4. Assign the correct Isodat method to the sequence.
5. Save the sequence file before starting.


## Running the Analysis

1. Verify carrier gas pressure (He > 500 psi, regulated to 50 psi).
2. Load capsules into the autosampler carousel in sequence order.
3. Press **Start Sequence** in Isodat.
4. Monitor the first 3--4 samples to confirm:
   - N~2~ and CO~2~ peaks are within the expected mass range
   - Peak shapes are symmetric and well-separated
   - Reference material $\delta$ values are within ±0.3‰ of expected
     values [@werner2001]
5. If values are drifting, stop the run, identify the cause, and
   restart after correction.


## Shutdown

1. After the final sample, allow the sequence to complete fully.
2. Follow the shutdown procedure in
   [SOP-L208](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd).
3. Export the raw data file from Isodat and save to the project
   directory.


## Data Reduction

Data reduction follows the protocol in
[SOP-L414](SOP-L414-soil-ea-irms.qmd), which covers:

1. Blank correction (empty tin capsule contributions) [@paul2007]
2. Linearity correction ($\delta$ vs. peak area regression)
3. Two-point scale normalization to the VPDB / AIR scale using
   certified RMs [@coplen2011]
4. Drift correction (linear regression through bracketing RMs)
5. Uncertainty estimation and quality flags


## Definitions of Certification Levels

| Level              | Capabilities                                           |
|:-------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI             | Unrestricted access; certify super-users               |
| Super-User         | Independent operation; certify certified users; replace He, O~2~ cylinders; change reactors |
| Certified User     | All steps from sample prep through data reduction; no unsupervised maintenance |
| Student Researcher | Sample prep and data reduction only, under supervision |

## Training Record

Before running analyses independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and [SOP-L208](SOP-L208-irms-general-instrument.qmd)
   in full
2. Be assigned a certification level by the Lab PI
3. Observe a Super-User or Certified User run a complete sequence
   from sample loading through data reduction
4. Run a supervised batch of at least 10 unknown samples with RM
   checks, achieving results within ±0.3‰ of expected values for
   both C and N
5. Be signed off by the Lab PI or designated Super-User
